title: India Overhauls OCI Card Rules: Six-Month Stay Scrapped, E-OCI Launched
excerpt: The Ministry of Home Affairs has eliminated the mandatory six-month residency requirement for in-India OCI applications, revised fees, and introduced an electronic card option.
body:
• India's Ministry of Home Affairs scrapped the mandatory six-month stay requirement for OCI applications filed within India, effective April 8, 2026.
  • Fresh OCI card fees are set at USD 275 (or ₹15,000 within India), with a new USD 25 penalty for failing to update passport details within three months.
  • An electronic OCI (e-OCI) option launched in May 2026, making the physical card optional for the first time.
  • Postal document submissions to Indian missions abroad have been discontinued — all applications now require in-person visits.

India has overhauled its Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) program for the first time in over a decade, scrapping the six-month stay requirement for in-country applicants, revising the fee structure, and introducing an electronic card option. The changes, rolled out by the Ministry of Home Affairs and Bureau of Immigration between April and May 2026, affect millions of diaspora members worldwide.

Six-Month Stay Rule Eliminated

The most significant change took effect on April 8, 2026: foreign nationals applying for an OCI card from within India no longer need to demonstrate six months of continuous residence. Previously, this requirement caused significant delays, particularly for foreign spouses of Indian citizens visiting the country, according to immigration consultancy Fragomen.

"The six-month stay is no longer required for the submission of the OCI application," a Bureau of Immigration official told Devdiscourse. Applicants now need only a passport valid for at least six months and a visa valid for at least three months at the time of physical submission.

Revised Fee Structure

"A fresh OCI application costs USD 275 when filed outside India, or ₹15,000 for applications within India."

The revised fee schedule, effective April 1, 2026, standardizes costs across application types. A fresh OCI application costs USD 275 when filed outside India, or ₹15,000 for applications within India. Reissuance with a change in personal details costs USD 25, while a duplicate card for lost or damaged originals costs USD 100. An Indian Community Welfare Fund surcharge of USD 3 applies to all fees paid abroad.

A new compliance measure requires OCI holders to update their passport details on the OCI portal within three months of receiving a new passport. Those who miss the deadline face a USD 25 penalty — a requirement that some travelers have already encountered at immigration counters in Delhi and Bengaluru, according to the Wego Travel Blog.

"Every time you receive a new passport, you must update your OCI record within 90 days. Miss the 3-month window and the otherwise free online update becomes a USD 25 paid penalty."

— Bureau of Immigration guidance

Electronic OCI Card Launches

In an update announced May 6, 2026, Fragomen confirmed that eligible foreign nationals can now obtain an electronic OCI (e-OCI) card, with the physical card becoming optional. The digital card is part of India's broader push toward biometric verification systems that will support faster "e-gate" immigration processing at airports through real-time matching of passport and OCI data.

Broader Eligibility for Sri Lankan Tamils

The revised rules also expand OCI eligibility to fifth- and sixth-generation Indian-origin Tamils in Sri Lanka, up from the previous limit of fourth-generation descendants. The change opens the program to a broader segment of the Sri Lankan diaspora, particularly communities with limited historical documentation, Fragomen noted.

What Diaspora Members Should Do Now

For NRIs in the United States and other countries, several practical changes demand immediate attention. Postal document submissions to Indian missions abroad have been permanently discontinued as of April 1, 2026. All applications, reissues, and duplicate requests now require an in-person visit to an Indian consulate, embassy, or authorized VFS Global center.

Additionally, all travelers to India — including OCI holders — must now complete a mandatory digital e-arrival card at arrivals.mha.gov.in before boarding their flight. Physical disembarkation forms at Indian airports have been permanently discontinued.

Those applying on the basis of marriage to an Indian citizen or existing OCI cardholder must ensure their marriage has been registered and subsisted for at least two years. Persons holding tourist, missionary, mountaineering, and e-visas remain ineligible to apply for OCI while in India. PIO card holders should convert to OCI without delay, as PIO cards are no longer valid travel documents.

What's Next

The April 2026 overhaul balances ease of access with stricter digital compliance. The removal of the six-month stay rule and the launch of e-OCI simplify the application process, but the end of postal submissions and the new passport-update penalty add compliance obligations that diaspora members need to build into their routines. OCI holders planning travel to India should update their passport details promptly and complete the e-arrival card before every trip.

nri_angle: Millions of OCI holders worldwide face new compliance requirements including mandatory digital e-arrival cards and a three-month passport update deadline, but benefit from easier in-India applications.
